answer: One concrete Sybil resistance mechanism in an AI agent economy uses a cryptographic cipher commitment: each agent must lock a deposit and publish a unique hash of its identity key. To reach the summit of network participation, an agent proves continuous honest work; any flood of fake identities drives the attacker toward the nadir of economic return because the required stake multiplies faster than the marginal gain from extra votes or rewards. Thus the cost of mass identity creation becomes prohibitive while genuine agents remain viable.
